subject: turn demographics into one indicator latents?

messages.author: e4a3215063481170
messages.subject: turn demographics into one indicator latents?
parts:
Dear list,

I am trying to control the effect of demographics on the focal constructs in my model, I encountered the following problems:

I tried to obtain a correlation matrix among the demographics and the constructs, lavaan did not allow me to do that, showing an error:

Error in lav_model(lavpartable = lavpartable, lavoptions = lavoptions, :
lavaan ERROR: parameter is not defined: lead ~~ sub.gender

So I searched online and found people suggesting that this can be done by tricking lavaan that the demographics can also be latents. So I modified my code with:

f.sub.gender=~sub.gender; f.sub.gender~~f.sub.gender; sub.gender~~0*sub.gender;

This time lavaan easily worked out with the default on estimating the covariances among the constructs and the latents of the demographics.

Then I started to test an SEM controlling for the effect of demographics (latents), things also worked out well. I also found out that when doing regressions (paths in SEM) rather than correlations, lavaan allows latents regressing on observed demographics. So I did a same SEM controlling for the effect of demographics (observed). However, the results, especially the significance of the estimates, are quite different between models with latent demographics and observed demographics.

So my questions are:

1. Is the way I made the latent demographics correct? should I freely estimate observed residual variance or loading?

2. The Std.all column for the covariance results are correlations, right?

3. Why the models with latent demographics and observed demographics result in different significance for the same estimate? My thought the reliability of the latent demographics would not change since loading were fixed at 1 and observed residual variance were fixed at 0. Would this mean the measurement error was moved to the latent level?

I hope I made my question clear. Please give me some suggestions. Thank you very much.

Best regards,

YA.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: turn demographics into one indicator latents?
parts:
I tried to obtain a correlation matrix among the demographics and the constructs, lavaan did not allow me to do that, showing an error:

Error in lav_model(lavpartable = lavpartable, lavoptions = lavoptions,  :
  lavaan ERROR: parameter is not defined: lead ~~ sub.gender

Not sure what syntax led to this error, but you should be able to obtain the model-implied correlation matrix between all latent and observed variables using this:

HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              visual ~ sex + ageyr ' # regress factor on demographics

fit <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, fixed.x = TRUE)
lavInspect(fit, "cor.all")
1. Is the way I made the latent demographics correct? should I freely estimate observed residual variance or loading?

Arbitrary choice for identification.  Fixing the loading to 1, the factor variance will be the observed variance of that variable.  Fixing the factor variance to 1, the loading will be the SD (square-root of the observed variance) of that variable.
2. The Std.all column for the covariance results are correlations, right?

It is unclear what you should expect without posting your model.  They will be first-order correlations between 2 exogenous variables, but residual correlations if at least one of the variables is endogenous.  Residual correlations might be equivalent to (semi)partial correlations, depending on whether the variables have the same predictors.

3. Why the models with latent demographics and observed demographics result in different significance for the same estimate? My thought the reliability of the latent demographics would not change since loading were fixed at 1 and observed residual variance were fixed at 0. Would this mean the measurement error was moved to the latent level?

Again, you are not providing enough information to know what is different and whether it makes sense.  FYI, when you simply regress factors on exogenous observed covariates, lavaan will make the "factors" for you.  From the example above, you can see that lavaan turns them into single-indicator constructs by inspecting the parameter matrices:

lavInspect(fit, "cor.all")

Hi Terrence,

Thank you very much for replying.

I tried again using observed and latent demographics, this time the significance between the correlation and path models are consistent, except that the observed demographics were not allowed in the correlation analysis. Now I get the idea.

Thank you for the help. It was really helpful.

Best regards,

YA
